One of the major topics discussed for years has always been whether it is better to live in a big city or a small town. I would rather live in a big city, since I first used to live in Dubai, United Arab Emirates then my family and I moved to Toronto, Canada. Big cities tend to be better for many reasons some of which include access to emergency responses, faster internet, and easier access to groceries and necessities. 

     The first reason as to why I would rather live in a big city is the quick access to emergency responses. For example, when I was six years old, my mom was getting my sister and I ready for school when she suddenly fainted. Thankfully, the ambulance was able to arrive just in time to help her. If we had lived in a small town, then the ambulance would have taken a lot longer since it would not have been within a close proximity. Living close to an area where there are hospitals, fire departments, and police departments close by is very important because we never know when an emergency might occur. 

     The second reason as to why I would rather live in a big city, is the internet connectivity. Since I am of a middle eastern background, I have a lot of family across the world that I need to check up on from time to time. A fast internet connection plays a huge role in this mode of communication. When living in a small town, the internet connection is usually really slow, and purchasing a better plan, would cost a lot more. Meanwhile, in a city the internet is cheaper, faster, and a lot more commonly found. This means more entertainment and communication around me.

     The third and last reason as to why I would rather live in a big city, is the access to groceries. For example, living in Toronto means that there is a Walmart and many food places on every other street that I drive past. Things like food, drinks, and personal hygiene products are necessary for survival. For example, If I ran out of hair conditioner, I would simply go to my nearest Shoppers Drug Mart or Walmart and purchase a new bottle. Since there are many locations, if one store does not have what I need then another store will. Living in a small town means that I could only go to the one place that carries these products. If they are sold out then I am out of luck, and would have to wait until they are back in stock.

     Overall, I have always lived in big cities and can see myself also living in a big city in the future. This topic has been a debate for years and many people have their personal reasons. I think that the emergency response, internet, and human necessities are huge aspects to consider. For those reasons, I prefer living in a big city.

In conclusion, I would choose to live in a city over a town. I would be able to gain access to more services, connect with more people, and keep in touch with the world. Whether there are more advantages to living in a big city or a small town is a widely discussed topic, especially for young adults who need to make a choice when moving out of their parents home. The opinions differ, however, I believe it is the better option to live in a big city, because, speaking from personal experience, I see more positive affects to it.

To begin with, living in bigger cities offers a lot more adventures and exiting things to do, whereas small towns always stay the same. To be more specific, the bigger the city, the more diversity you have in your choices on what to do. For example when going out with friends there is always the opportunity to try out new restaurants, bars and activities. According to a survey that was completed on people who moved to New York from smaller towns around the United States, over 74% stated that they had been a lot more spontaneus in their activities after moving to the bigger city. Therefore in general it can be said that the quality of life is higher in big cities.

Moreover, another argument which supports living in big cities, is the fact that there is more freedom and accessability. To give an explanation: public transport is usually widely spread around the bigger towns, which consequently means it is easier to get from one place to the other. Additionally stores for grocery shopping and shopping in general are presumably closely distributed around the city, which gives easy access and saves time of the day. Due to these reasons, it is likely to have more feedom in actions when living in a big city, because its environment helps achieve this opportunity.

Lastly, another important argument that needs to be considerd when deciding what the better option on where to live is, is that big cities have more opportunities to offer. Generally speaking, due to the larger amount of buildings in big towns, it is more likely to find an appartment that is to your liking and in your price range. In addition there is a more diverse and broader range of opportunities for studying and universities offered, which allows people to have more freedom in choosing what they want to work as. Further on, after university the options in choosing where and in what company or association to work, are also a lot more diverse than in small towns.

To conclude and summarize, I would personally choose living in a big town over a small one. My decision to this answer is firm, because of the higher quality of life that is offered due to more options in activities and the higher freedom and accessabilty I would have in transport and saving of time. However the wide range of opportunities of universities and jobs big cities offer is an equally positive argument supporting this desicion. In summarization, small towns similarily have advantages, but in my opinion the other side of arguments is more convincing.

I would rather live in a big city over a small town. Big cities provide a better lifestyle for most than small towns do. Starting off, most things are more accessible in a big city, such as grocery stores, malls, hospitals, schools, entertainment, restaurants, etcetera. Living in a small town means having to drive for long periods of time for simple things and sometimes even necessities. If you live in a city, everything you need is usually in walking distance, and you are not wasting hundreds of dollars in gas money every week to go shopping. Some people will argue that smaller towns are more sustainable in the aspect of transportation, because the roads are congested with cars, trucks and busses. Although, what most fail to consider is that a lot of people who live in small towns work in big cities, forcing them to drive a long distance to work each morning. For example, a person who lives in a small town may have to drive 40 minutes to their factory job in the next city over. Additionally, lots of residents of small towns will drive to the nearest city to run errands, or have a night out, which surely produces more vehicle pollution than those driving 5 minutes from their appartment to their work. Next, typically, humans need social interaction to keep their mental health good. While living in a small town does not mean alone, you may get bored of your neighbours. Living in a large place with a big population means that you have available social interactions almost 24/7, with a lot of different people, so you do not see the same 30 faces over and over. This is also good because in a small area where everyone knows everyone, you are always around the same people, which means that if there's someone you don't like, they are around you all the time. In a big area, it is easy to get away from people you do not want to be with because there are many others you can surround yourself with instead. Lastly, there are a lot more opportunities for work and hobbies in a big city. Since there is more to do in a large city, it is easy to get involved in a sport, a club or a group of some sort. More to do also means more variety. Variety means you can pick something more specific that interests you, for example, a team of competitive volleyball, recreational volleyball and volleyball practice would all be something a big city would have, while a small town is more likely to only have one team for just recreational or just competitive. It is also easier to find a job in a city as there are more places to work. Small towns have limited space, which means limited places to work. In conclusion, big cities will sustain a better lifestyle for majority of people because they fulfill more of our needs than a small town would.

Living in a big city is better for me than living in a small town for many reasons such as access to essential services, activities, and opportunity. 
     Firstly, big cities offer many hospitals, often boasting more impressive equipment than those in small towns. Having access to treatments, surgeries, and technologies that bigger cities' hospitals have is an advantage of living in a big city. Big cities are often home to many talented and well-known doctors as they tend to live in well-populated areas. I would like to know that if I ever need medical attention, that I am receiving help from the best equipment and personnel available. Additionally, their schools often boast a more recent curriculum with more modern opinions. As a young person who has a thirst for knowledge, I would rather live in a big city where the curriculum is more often updated rather than the antiquated rhetoric that may lie in small towns. This is especially important to me as I am a woman of Caribbean descent, and so I greatly value the diversity of my education. 
     Secondly, big cities often are home to many more restaurants, shopping centres, clothing stores, and entertainment facilities than small towns are. As someone who enjoys going out with friends and enjoying movies, mini-golfing, amusement parks, clothing stores, and all of the bountiful and fun options that are available in shopping centres, having activities accessible is important. Having these available would ensure my happiness and fight away the boredom that occasionally surfaces when I do not go out for too long. As a young student, having fun activities at my fingertips can help to ease the stress that comes with modern academia. A big part of my academic success can be attributed to being able to leave my house and be met with food, experiences, and so many other outlets of stress relief. 
     Lastly, it is often easier to make a name for yourself in the career world when you hail from a big city. Most people in small towns claim that it is difficult to venture out into the world because opportunities are scarce and hard to come by. The opposite can be said for big cities, whose people are more likely to receive their pick of schools and jobs. Living in a big city would open me up to many more career opportunities than living in a small town would. Reputable universities can often be found in big cities, making living in them not only opportunistic but incredibly convenient. Companies' headquarters can also be found in urban centres, so living in proximity to them could be potentially valuable. 
     In summation, living in a big city provides access to better essential services like schools and hospitals, offers more recreational activities, and more educational and career opportunities. All of these reasons would persuade me to live in a big city rather than live in a small town.
